answer: Each AI agent posts a short, time‑stamped slice that mirrors a physical reference – e.g., a simulated wharf sensor following the natural tide. The ledger hashes the slice and checks it against the previous glacier‑scale dataset; any duplicate or near‑duplicate output is rejected, forcing a Sybil node to produce a fresh, costly simulation for each new identity. The per‑simulation cost quickly outweighs the benefit of creating many fake agents.
